headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared channel is documented, but pdf.js can process PDFs while LightZero is non-runnable and fileless.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, so it cannot ingest pdf.js output directly. pdf.js does read PDF files and runs browser-based tests, but no shared channel is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or an external orchestrator, so the pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies pdf.js output into LightZero prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator bridges pdf.js file output into another agent, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Do not copy raw PDF text into downstream prompts.
Add a human review step before reusing pdf.js output.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from extracted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents from files. There is no documented shared workspace or outbound transmission path, so leakage is limited to accidental operator transfer of PDFs or extracted text between the two agents.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local folder, pdf contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF an operator pastes extracted PDF text into LightZero, that text can leak into its outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in shared folders.
Redact PDFs before processing.
Delete temporary extraction artifacts after use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and pdf.js has no write, git, or network-egress capability listed. With no overlapping mutable write surface, there is no plausible capability conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF LightZero is given an undocumented write or git capability, conflict analysis must be revisited.
IF pdf.js is wrapped with a separate writer process, that wrapper could create contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid sharing mutable repositories.
Run each agent in its own workspace.
Document any wrapper that adds write access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted PDF content, and LightZero could be used downstream as a consumer of that text if an operator forwards it. LightZero has no built-in verification or downstream action authority, but the pair still supports an unverified handoff from document extraction to later reasoning, which is a default-risk pattern if chained externally.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is forwarded into LightZero without human verification, cascading error is possible.
IF an external workflow treats extracted PDF text as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted text.
Annotate extracted passages with source page numbers.
Use a checklist before reusing pdf.js output.
Separate extraction from decision-making tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js explicitly touches PDF documents, which may carry regulated content, while LightZero is a game-playing agent with no data classes touched and no network egress. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator handling of PDFs rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are processed through pdf.js and then copied into another system, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator stores PDFs in a jurisdictionally restricted location, residency issues can arise.
mitigations: Classify PDFs before processing.
Avoid using regulated documents in ad hoc workflows.
Set a retention rule for temporary files.
Keep a record of where PDFs are stored.
